About Event
​Have a game idea you want to bring to life? Join us for a 4h Game Jam in the heart of SF.

​We kick things off in San Francisco on Wednesday evening with four hours of in-person building, food, and good company. The theme stays secret until kickoff, so come with an open mind and leave with a playable game.

​Whether you’re a seasoned game dev, a designer, an artist, a sound person, or someone who has never shipped a game before, you’re welcome. Bring a laptop, bring friends, or find your team on the night.

​Any engine, any tools, any genre. AI tools are fair game, and our sponsors’ platforms are a great way to move fast on voice, music, 3D assets, and in-browser prototyping. The only rule: the game has to be built during the jam and fit the theme.

​Schedule:

​4:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, and team formation

​5:00 PM: Kickoff, sponsor intros, and the theme reveal

​5:20 PM: Building starts

​8:30 PM: Building stops

​9:00 PM: Winners Announced

​How it works

​Build a game, solo or in a team of up to 4. The five highest-rated games advance to the judges, who select the top three.

​Your judges:

​Cristi Dragan - Growth @ Weekend

​Thao Chi Vu - Product Designer @ Roadrunner

​Pantelis Kalogiros - General Partner @ Exponential

​Luize Darta Sietina - CEO @ Crowdable

​Two Tracks: Party Games Track and Random Games Track

​Party Games Track, Weekend:
We’re hosting the Party Games Track, looking for the next big living-room hit! Think multiplayer party games designed for the big screen, ideally for 2–6 players, where everyone joins by scanning a QR code on the TV and uses their phone as a controller.

​We want games that make the room come alive! Think shouting, laughing, moving around, friendly competition, and unforgettable moments. The kind of gameplay that’s so entertaining people can’t resist pulling out their phones to share it on Instagram Stories, Snapchat, or TikTok.

​The winning team will be invited to pitch their game to Weekend’s product and engineering teams and get feedback from the people behind our growing portfolio of TV games!

​Random Games Track:
Anything goes. Platformers, puzzlers, roguelikes, narrative experiments, cozy sims, or something nobody has a genre name for yet. If it’s fun, surprising, and fits the theme, it belongs here.

​About The Sponsors:

​Chroma Awards: The Chroma Awards is a creator-led competition for Film, Music Videos, Ads, and Games. Incubated by ElevenLabs, Season 2 features $200k+ in cash prizes across 6 tracks, and is open to submissions between October 19, 2026 and January 1, 2027. This event is hosted under the Chroma Awards umbrella and the #1 winner is fast-tracked to the semi-finals of their chosen submission category.

​

​ElevenLabs: ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.The company builds three platforms: ElevenAgents for businesses deploying voice and chat agents at scale, ElevenCreative for creators and marketers generating and editing speech, music, images and video in 70+ languages, and ElevenAPI giving developers access to its audio AI models.

​

​Meshy: Where ideas take shape in 3D. Meshy helps 12M+ creators, developers, and studios turn a prompt or image into a detailed 3D model in minutes, ready for real-time engines, 3D printing, or product visualization.

​

​Rosebud AI: Rosebud AI Game Maker helps people turn ideas into playable games. Describe what you imagine, build it in your browser, and share it with others.

​

​Weekend is turning TVs into gaming consoles with 20+ games, from legendary franchises like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and The Price Is Right to exciting originals like Spot On and Sketchy AF.

​

​Prizes

​1st place: Fast-tracked to the semi-finals of the Chroma Awards in your chosen category.

​Party Games Track winner: Pitch your game to Weekend’s product and engineering teams

​Every participant will receive 1 month of ElevenLabs Creator Plan + A free month of Meshy Pro.

​Join in person

​📍Hosted by Open Austria San Francisco. Exact address shared with approved guests.

​Spots are limited to 70, so register early and cancel if you know you can't show up anymore. See you Wednesday.

About Event

About Event
Welcome to the Post-Training & RL Buildathon — a one-day, in-person gathering in San Francisco for engineers, AI builders, founders, and researchers who want to spend a full day building with post-training techniques: SFT, RLHF/RLAIF, DPO/GRPO, reward modeling, RL environments, evals, and agentic fine-tuning.
Hosted by Devnovate in collaboration with AWS, the day pairs hands-on building with a panel of practitioners from fast-growing AI companies who are putting RL and post-training into production.
Event Details
When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, Thursday, 30 October 2026

Where: San Francisco, CA

Format: One-day in-person buildathon + practitioner panel

Who: ML engineers, AI builders, founders, researchers, data scientists, and technology professionals

Theme: Post-training & reinforcement learning

What to Expect
A full day dedicated to building on post-training and RL

Panel: “RL in Production” with engineers from TinyFish, and other leading AWS customers

Mentorship from experienced ML practitioners and AWS solution architects

AWS credits, partner credits, and challenge prizes

Access to modern AI tools, APIs, GPUs, and developer resources

Live demos and project showcases at the end of the day

Food, refreshments, swag, and prizes

What Can You Build?
Anything that uses post-training or RL to make a model or agent better:
Fine-tune an open-weight model on a domain dataset (SFT DPO GRPO)

Build a reward model or RL environment for an agentic task

Train an agent with RL to use tools, browse, or complete multi-step workflows

Design evals and preference datasets for alignment or task performance

Optimize inference-time behavior with learned policies

Or something nobody has tried before

Bring an idea, a dataset, a model you want to improve — or just the desire to build. Find teammates, get feedback, and ship something real by the end of the day.
Who Should Join?
Whether you’re an ML engineer shipping fine-tuned models, a researcher exploring RL for agents, a founder testing an AI product, or a student getting into post-training — you’re welcome. You don’t need to be an expert. You just need to be ready to build.
Come with a model. Leave with a better one.

About Event

Join top AI engineers, founders, and builders at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco for a full day of building production-ready AI agents powered by live web data.
Special Halloween themed tracks and Best Costume Prize
Build on You.com developer platform, Parasail, One, and Crewai and collaborate directly with the engineers behind the APIs to ship something real and SPOOKY in a single day.
Why Attend?
Build alongside Bay Area's top AI engineers, founders, and builders

Learn directly from You.com 's product and engineering leaders

Get hands-on help from the engineers behind the APIs powering Agentic Era

Ship a working prototype in one day and demo your project to AI leaders and judges

Expand your network with some of the Bay Area's best

Register on the AWS portal to enter the venue. This is separate from your Luma registration, and it's required. AWS security checks names at the door against its own list, so please complete this step in advance.
Register here: http://events.builder.aws.com/d/bczz8z
It takes about 2 minutes. If you've already done this, you're all set.
Building rules
Bring a valid physical photo ID. Digital IDs aren't accepted at check-in.

No scooters, bikes, or non-ADA motorized vehicles inside the building, and there's no bike or scooter parking on-site. If you're riding in, plan to use public parking nearby.

Address: AWS Builder Loft, 525 Market Stentrance, 2nd floor, San Francisco.

Themes
🧟 Theme 1: "The Exorcism Protocol" (Autonomous Agent Swarms)
A paranormal outbreak is spreading through a live facility simulation. Teams build an autonomous supervised swarm — CrewAI agents with distinct roles, tools, and only partial individual knowledge — that must sense, share intel, and coordinate containment in real time. Victory is measured by the swarm, not a single model: containment speed, false-alarm rate, and "civilians saved" all feed the live venue scoreboard.
🎃 Theme 2: The "Haunted Dashboard" (Generative UI Pipelines)
Create an automated Spooky Tactical Command Station served by Parasail's inference endpoints. The system takes real-time, unstructured "Spooky Incident Logs" (e.g., zombie outbreaks, phantom activity levels) and processes them through a structured retrieval network to dynamically build and compile functional, beautifully designed web interfaces on the fly over WebSockets.

The top teams compete for a stacked prize pool of $10k+ from You.com and our partners.

​Prepare the Planet
​Humanity has discovered a new world capable of sustaining life—but the planet is unstable, unfinished, and rapidly becoming uninhabitable.

​A specialized crew of Space Monkeys, supported by autonomous AI machines, has been deployed ahead of the human fleet. Their mission: transform this untamed world into a functioning civilization in only 10 days.

​They must build the intelligence, infrastructure, financial systems, culture, governance, and defenses humanity will need to survive.

​Each day marks a new stage of planetary development. Every challenge reflects a real frontier facing AI, blockchain, robotics, creators, founders, investors, and policymakers.

​The Mission Begins

​10 Days to Prepare a Planet for Humanity

​Days 1–3 — Build the Planet
Hackathon teams deploy the systems humanity will depend on, including energy, artificial intelligence, communications, robotics, water, digital identity, and decentralized infrastructure.

​Days 5–8 — Design Civilization
Speakers, founders, investors, creators, and policymakers determine how intelligence, ownership, culture, capital, and governance should operate in this new world.

​Day 9 — The Allocation
Selected founders present their technologies to the Planetary Allocation Council for investment, strategic partnerships, and real-world deployment.

​Day 10 — Humanity Arrives
The entire ecosystem comes together for a final networking experience designed to activate the new civilization and welcome humanity’s arrival.

​DAY 1-3 — BUILD THE PLANET HACKATHON - JULY 17-19

​Builders, designers, and developers collaborate to create next-generation AI, autonomous systems, and decentralized technologies.

​Over four days, teams will form, build, and refine their solutions with support from expert mentors, then showcase their innovations to judges, investors, and industry leaders for awards, recognition, and potential partnership opportunities.

​Rules:

​Participants will use AI agents to build and expand a procedurally generated version of Planet ZekNova.

​Choose one of four biomes—Forest, Desert, Highlands, or Arctic—each offering unique resources, challenges, and strategic advantages.

​The team with the most advanced and functional biome by Day 4 wins.

​We don't have any prizes unless someone wants to sponsor the hackathon. Instead you'll win street cred. Which is a email blast to our massive network of builders and investors.

​Winners will be selected by the governamce system. Voted on by all AI x Crypto Expo attendees.

​Scout Planet ZekNova

​DAY 4 — FRONTIER INTELLIGENCE - JULY 20

​Days 4–8: Speaker Series

​Four days of keynotes, panels, workshops, and expert conversations exploring the technologies and systems shaping the next generation of civilization.

​Bharathi Raja Ramachandra Bose

​Vice President, Genpact

​Talk: What Are Consulting Companies Doing in the AI Revolution?

​Bharathi explores how consulting firms are helping enterprises move from AI experimentation to scalable deployment. The session will address enterprise architecture, data modernization, responsible governance, workforce transformation, intelligent copilots, and measurable business value.

​Anupriya Ramraj

​CEO and Co-Founder, Vaultzy

​Talk: AI Agents, Blockchain & the Future of Human Credentials

​Anupriya explores how agentic AI, blockchain, and verifiable digital credentials can create a trusted foundation for the AI era. The session will examine applications across employment, education, healthcare, financial services, and government, with a focus on trust, accessibility, and opportunities for underserved communities.

​Deepali Gosain

​Founder and CEO, Ferendis

​Workshop: Is Your AI High-Risk? A Hands-On Compliance Classification Workshop

​Deepali guides founders and product teams through classifying real AI use cases using the EU AI Act as an anchor. Participants will identify applicable requirements across SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, HIPAA, and related frameworks, prioritize key controls, and leave with a documented first-pass compliance plan.

​Himanshu Goel

​AI Researcher, Independent AI Researcher

​Talk: Beyond Hallucinations: Building Trustworthy RAG Systems for Finance and Crypto

​Himanshu examines how RAG systems can produce confident but ungrounded answers in high-stakes financial and crypto environments. He will share architectural methods for improving retrieval accuracy, reducing embedding costs, and building more trustworthy AI systems.

​DAY 5 — BLOCKCHAIN STACK - JULY 21
​Fernando Jia

​Co-Founder and CEO, Intelligence Cubed (i³)

​Talk: Make AI Auditable: Watermark Provenance as the Payment Rails for AI

​Fernando explores how watermark-based provenance, on-chain attestations, and automated settlement can transform AI outputs into verifiable economic transactions. The session examines attribution, usage-based billing, derivative ownership, and automated royalties.

​Srinivasan Sriram

​Founder & CEO

​Talk: Unlocking DeFi Liquidity for RWAs

​Srinivasan explores how emerging infrastructure can unlock DeFi liquidity for tokenized real-world assets. The session will examine KYC restrictions, custody-related tax implications, and the financial plumbing needed to help RWA holders access liquidity while using yield-generating assets as collateral.

​Vadim Khramov

​Founder and Chief Investment Officer, Edge Capital Investment Management Ltd

​Talk: Beyond Beta: Institutional Yield Strategies in Digital Assets

​Vadim explores how institutional allocators are moving beyond passive crypto exposure into market-neutral, liquid, and risk-adjusted yield strategies. The discussion will address portfolio construction, capital efficiency, liquidity deployment, custody, and regulated structures.

​Karnika Yashwant

​Founder, KEY Difference

​Talk: AI Agents Are the New Degens

​Karnika examines what happens when autonomous agents begin routing liquidity, managing yield, rebalancing portfolios, evaluating protocols, and executing trades around the clock. The session explores the implications for trust, permissions, reputation, risk, and market infrastructure.

​DAY 6 — CREATOR ECONOMY - JULY 22
​Manish Jain

​Founder and Thinker, SystemsWay Academy

​Talk: Understanding Understanding: The One Skill Creators Need in the Age of AI

​Manish explores why the most valuable skill in the AI era may no longer be accessing knowledge, but determining whether what we believe we understand is genuine understanding. The session challenges creators and builders to distinguish reliable knowledge from pseudo-understanding, persuasive explanations, and confidently presented nonsense.

About Event

Claude Cowork for Lawyers & Paralegals: Hands-On Workshop
Built for practicing lawyers and paralegals, this workshop shows you how to use Claude in your day-to-day legal work—from contract review and NDA triage to meeting preparation and first drafts.
We'll cover three things: skills that teach Claude your firm's playbooks and drafting style, connectors that connect it to your email, calendar, and documents, and the latest Claude features relevant to legal practice.
You'll see practical demonstrations of legal workflows, then work through a task yourself. We'll also discuss confidentiality, privilege, and the points where professional judgment and review remain essential.
No technical background needed. Bring a laptop and a task from your practice that you'd like to speed up. You'll leave with a workflow you can put to use Monday morning.
This workshop is designed for lawyers, paralegals, and other legal professionals. Priority registration will be given to those working in the legal profession.

Organizers
Max Krueger is the founder of Backland Labs , an AI studio that helps organizations apply artificial intelligence to complex business workflows. A self-taught AI engineer and former startup CTO, Max has led engineering teams, built production AI systems, and advised Fortune 500 companies. He also runs a growing AI community in San Diego, bringing together practitioners to share knowledge and explore practical uses of AI.

Julian Bryant is a San Diego attorney and software developer who uses AI in his own legal practice every day. A Georgetown Law graduate, Cooley alum, and former startup founder with a decade of app development behind him, he brings a rare blend of legal and technical fluency to the question of what AI can actually do for lawyers. Julian is also the Lead Organizer of Startup Weekend San Diego.
